text:
sara: Noticing a lot of customers scrap together error parsing because all SDKs return ApiError. Can we formalize typed errors and a small wire contract?

mike: Yes. Current SDK surface forces string parsing of messages. Pain points: 1) Retry-After header formats differ, 2) 401 vs 403 confusion, 3) streams don't surface typed failures.

olga: Minimal wire contract suggestion: always include `code` (string) and `message` in JSON body, plus standard Retry-After header when applicable. Example body: {"code": "rate_limit", "message": "quota exceeded", "meta": {"retry_after": 30}}. SDKs map code+status -> typed error.

trent: Runtime surface: expose typed exceptions (RateLimitError, AuthExpiredError, PermissionDeniedError, TransientServerError, BadRequestError, StreamError). Each should expose `status_code`, `code`, `retry_after_seconds` (optional), and `is_retryable` boolean.

sara: For streaming, include `partial_bytes` or `tokens_emitted` on StreamError so callers can offer resume. Also include the raw body as `raw` but redact auth-related fields.

mike: Language specifics: Python/TS - class errors; Go - interface with accessors (RetryAfter() (time.Duration, bool), IsRetryable() bool). Keep names consistent across SDKs.

olga: Migration: server emits `code` for a deprecation window; SDKs add typed classes behind minor-version flag; keep old ApiError for backward compatibility. Add e2e tests that assert parsing of both `Retry-After: 120` and HTTP-date forms.

trent: Add quick-snippets in docs: handle rate-limit by checking `RateLimitError.retry_after_seconds`, refresh on `AuthExpiredError`, and show permission scope from `error.meta.scope` on `PermissionDeniedError`.

ci-bot: CI: created branch error-typed-exceptions by mike -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/compare/error-typed-exceptions

sara: Great. Mike/Olga — please draft the RFC with a compatibility mapping table and short examples for each language. I'll coordinate the rollout notes.
